FAQ

Questions, answered

The short version of what people ask. Each answer links to where the detail lives.

The game

What is ApexSim?

A racing simulator built around one authoritative physics server: a 420 Hz simulation in Rust that every car, yours included, is drawn from by an Unreal Engine 5 client. It ships with 17 cars and 29 real-world circuits. What it simulates.

What does it cost?

Nothing for personal, non-commercial use. ApexSim is source-available, not open source: you may download, run, study and modify it for yourself under the ApexSim licence. Selling it, redistributing it or running it as a paid or public service needs a commercial licence.

Where do I get it?

From the releases page: unzip it and run launcher.exe, which starts the game and, if you want one, a local server.

Is it finished?

No: it is in active development and changes often. What is not built yet is listed openly in the simulation gaps and the roadmap.

Why do the cars and circuits have unusual names?

The cars are fictional, and the circuits carry names of their own rather than anyone's trademark. The layouts themselves are measured from the real circuits.

Hardware

What do I need to run it?

Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit, x64), a DirectX 12 graphics card and 16 GB of RAM. Full system specs.

Does it run on Mac, Linux or Windows on Arm?

The game runs on 64-bit x64 Windows only; Windows on Arm (Snapdragon) is not supported. A dedicated server runs on Windows or, in Docker, on Linux.

Which wheels work?

DirectInput wheels, pedals and button boxes, with force feedback worked out from the tyres and scaled to your wheelbase's peak torque. A gamepad or a keyboard works too.

Triple screens? VR?

Triple screens yes, with the side views toed in to match your rig. VR is not supported yet.

Racing

Can I race offline?

Yes: races, weekends and whole seasons against AI drivers at a level you choose, hotlaps against your own ghost, and the driving school.

Can I race online?

Yes. Someone hosts a server (the launcher can start one, or run it on its own) and the others join it by address. There is no public server list yet.

What does hosting take?

The server, the same content as the players, and two ports open: 9000/TCP and 9001/UDP. An operator dashboard runs the sessions.

Is the physics on my PC?

No. The server simulates every car and enforces every rule: collisions, track limits, the pit lane, assists. Your game draws what it says.

Content

Do I need Assetto Corsa?

No. ApexSim comes with its own cars and circuits. If you do own Assetto Corsa, you can bring its cars and tracks across.

How do I import my Assetto Corsa cars and tracks?

In the launcher, Manage content > Import from Assetto Corsa, then pick a car or track folder, or a whole folder of them. It needs Python 3.11 or newer the first time. How it works and what converts.

Is importing Assetto Corsa content allowed?

The importers convert content you already own, on your own machine, for your own use, and nothing they make is shared or uploaded by ApexSim. Respect the game's terms and each mod author's; content encrypted by Custom Shaders Patch is refused. ApexSim is not affiliated with or endorsed by the makers of Assetto Corsa, and you use the importers at your own risk.

Can I make my own cars, circuits or HUD?

Yes: they are files the game reads at runtime, with a guide for each. Modding.

How do I share what I made?

As a content pack: one file the other player installs from the launcher's Manage content.

Source

Can I build it from source?

Yes, on Windows with Rust, Python 3 and Unreal Engine 5.8: ./scripts/initialize_content.ps1 once, then ./scripts/play_editor.ps1 -Build. The build guide has the rest.

Can I use it for a commercial league or event?

Paid events, public or paid servers and use inside a business need a commercial licence; the licence says how to ask for one.
